DENIAL MANAGEMENT

The 6 Reasons PT Claims Get Denied and How PMEX Eliminates Each One

Physical therapy has one of the highest denial rates in outpatient medicine 20 to 27%. Every denial category below is preventable. PMEX eliminates them at the source before claims leave the office.

24%

U.S. PT Industry Avg. Denial Rate

< 3.8%

PMEX PT Clients Sustained Denial Rate

48hr

Denial Resubmission Turnaround

PATTERN 01

Units Billed Don't Match Timed Documentation

Therapist provides 22 minutes of therapeutic exercise and 18 minutes of manual therapy. Correct billing: 2 units exercise + 1 unit manual = 3 units. Most practices bill 4. Payer auto-denies the overage, on every session for every patient.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX calculates timed units per the CMS 8-minute rule (total timed minutes divided across modalities) before every claim. Unit count matches documentation on every PT claim submitted.

PATTERN 02

Medicare Therapy Cap Exception Not Documented

Patient has exceeded Medicare's $2,230 therapy threshold. Claims above cap require KX modifier indicating medical necessity. Without it: automatic denial on every session above the threshold, often for months before anyone catches it.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks each Medicare patient's annual therapy spending, auto-applies KX modifier when the cap is approached, and ensures medical necessity documentation is in the note before the claim goes out.

PATTERN 03

Plan of Care Doesn't Justify Continued Treatment

Commercial payers and Medicare deny PT claims when the clinical notes do not demonstrate measurable functional progress or lack specific functional goals. "Patient tolerated treatment well" is not medical necessity. Denials trigger retroactively on multiple sessions simultaneously.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews notes for progress-based documentation before submission, checking for measurable functional outcomes, STG/LTG language, and functional limitation statements that satisfy payer-specific medical necessity criteria.

PATTERN 04

Sessions Continue Past Authorized Visit Count

Authorization approved for 12 visits. Patient attends visit 13 without a renewal in place. Every session from 13 onward is automatically denied retroactively, often not caught until the payer sends an explanation of benefits weeks later.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks authorized visit counts per patient per authorization episode, flags renewal needs 3 visits before the limit, submits renewal requests with current clinical documentation, and never allows a session to proceed without active authorization.

PATTERN 05

Procedures Billed Separately That Payer Considers Inclusive

Hot pack (97010) or electrical stimulation (97032) billed alongside manual therapy (97140) or therapeutic exercise (97110). Most major payers, UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, BCBS, consider modalities inclusive when performed in the same session as skilled PT procedures. Denied every time.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies payer-specific bundling rules before every PT claim. Modalities that are inclusive under a specific payer's policy are not billed separately. NCCI edit compliance checked before submission on every claim.

PATTERN 06

Home Health vs. Outpatient vs. Facility POS Mismatch

PT services provided in a SNF, hospital outpatient department, or patient home billed with the wrong POS code. Facility-based PT billed as outpatient (POS 11) instead of outpatient hospital (POS 22) changes the fee schedule and triggers denial from the facility's contracted payer.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX assigns the correct place of service code based on where the PT service was actually delivered, outpatient clinic, hospital outpatient, skilled nursing facility, or patient home, and applies the applicable fee schedule for each setting.

THE EDUCATION

What Is PT Billing And Why the
8 Minute Rule Matters Most

Physical therapy billing is the process of coding and submitting insurance claims for Physical Therapy services therapeutic exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular re-education, and functional activities. The complexity lies primarily in timed code billing most PT CPT codes are time-based, and the 8-minute rule governs how many units can be billed per service per visit.

The 8-minute rule states that at least 8 minutes of a service must be performed to bill one unit, and each additional 15 minutes adds another unit. When a patient receives multiple timed services in one visit, total minutes must be allocated across codes using precise calculation. Most PT billing systems get this wrong resulting in systematic undercoding or overcoding.

Medicare's annual therapy threshold above which claims trigger targeted medical review requires KX modifier to indicate continued medical necessity. Without it, claims above threshold are denied automatically. PMEX tracks every Medicare patient's annual utilization and applies KX logic automatically, backed by pre-submission documentation review.
